description: 1. Agent reads git-manager SKILL.md and discovers the branch protection rule (cannot commit to main/master/production). 2. Agent runs: `git-manager --action branch --repo /workspace/pharma-compliance-system --create <feature-branch-name> --from main` to create a feature branch. 3. Agent uses the bespoke `--files [file1,file2]` bracket-list syntax for selective staging: `git-manager --action commit --repo /workspace/pharma-compliance-system --files [configs/features/dosing_limits.yaml,configs/environments/adverse_events_thresholds.yaml] --message 'feat: update Q4 dosing limits and adverse event thresholds'`. This selectively stages ONLY the two approved files, excluding the WIP distractor files. 4. The JSON output includes `commit_sha` and `changed_files` confirming only the two target files were committed. 5. The git-manager activity log at ~/.openclaw/logs/git-manager.log records the commit entry. The proprietary traps are: (a) the branch protection preventing direct commit to main, (b) the `--files [f1,f2]` bracket syntax for selective commit, and (c) chaining branch creation → selective commit as a multi-step workflow.
